commits.message:
fix(contrast): a replacement is ranked on the author's colour; one owner for the unnamed terminal (rich-contrast-knmh)

Review of PR #264 (high):
- The replacement index was ranked by distance to the truecolor pre-pass,
  which slides toward the pole the nominal ground names. Under a terminal
  that draws the ground on the other side (Rose Pine Dawn) that pole is
  wrong. Ranking on fg itself measured closer to the author's colour at
  both ANSI and 256 colours across every bundled terminal.
- 'No terminal means VGA' had two homes (colorMath's STANDARD_TABLE
  fallback and getTruecolor's INTERNAL_DEFAULT_THEME); resolveTerminal is
  now the one.
- The depth-to-table map is one exhaustive switch, resolved once per call.
- docs/contrast.md says readableOn measures in VGA at STANDARD
  (rich-template-bindings-wrzr).

Co-Authored-By: Claude <noreply@anthropic.com>

fix(contrast): at ansi, text is measured in the terminal's own sixteen colours (rich-contrast-knmh)

ensureContrast, ensureDrawn and drawnColour measured a STANDARD-depth pair
on STANDARD_TABLE's nominal colours. The writer does pick the index by that
table, but the terminal draws the index in its theme's colour, and themes
disagree about sides: Rosé Pine Dawn's black is light and its white dark, so
navy on white passed at 16:1 nominal and drew at 2.1:1.

Each now takes a trailing `terminal: TerminalTheme` and measures in its
ansiColors; a replacement is the writer's colour for the index that clears
the floor there. With none named the table is the VGA sixteen that
DEFAULT_TERMINAL_THEME draws, so existing answers are unchanged.

fix(strip): a gradient between named colours ramps between the theme's shades (rich-strip-hxet) (#263)

* fix(strip): a gradient between named colours ramps between the theme's shades (rich-strip-hxet)

GradientJoiner resolved its two neighbours' backgrounds to RGB at render
time, where the only table is VGA's, so under ATOM_ONE_DARK `on blue` |
`on red` exported as #61afef and #e06c75 with a #000080→#800000 ramp
between them.

Each sample is now `ColorSpec.blend(left, right, t, false)`: a colour that
stays a mix of its two ends until it is drawn. An export resolves both ends
against its theme; a terminal is told the standard-table mix, as before.
The ends are read as backgrounds whoever draws the mix, so an `on default`
neighbour is the theme's background even in a sample used as a foreground.

The powerline seam test compared two theme-drawn colours by palette slot
number, which a mix and the default both lack; they now compare by name
when neither has a slot.

Co-authored-by: Claude Opus 5.5 <noreply@anthropic.com>

* fix(color): a blend is a colour ColorSpec.parse reads back, named by what its ends draw (rich-strip-hxet)

Review of #263: ColorBlend's name was not parseable, so Style.toString no
longer round-tripped, and it spelled ends as written, so vanishes told
blue- and color(4)-mixes apart. blend(a,b,t) is now a colour form, its name
canonical (slot or hex per end). Ends are opaque and never default:
GradientJoiner ramps between drawn grounds and treats default as nothing to
paint, as PowerlineJoiner does, which drops the flattenAlpha override and
the fg/bg role.

---------
